metric.why: Capex is the audited ground truth beneath every buildout headline. This site reads it directly from EDGAR company facts, quarterly, for the hyperscalers and the largest colocation operators.
metric.definition: Quarterly capital spending reported to the SEC by the companies building the facilities, tracked on this page from each company's own XBRL filings.

reading.body:
Quarterly capital expenditure filings from SEC EDGAR are the most reliable single signal of how fast hyperscalers and colocation operators are actually building, because they are audited, standardized, and reported under legal obligation rather than press release.

Capex is upstream of everything else in the AI supply chain. A data center cannot be built without spending appearing in these filings first, and that spending precedes rack deployment, power draw, and ultimately compute availability by months or years. Watching this number across the named companies in aggregate reveals whether announced buildout intentions are being funded or deferred.

What this metric does not cover: it says nothing about where the money is going, whether toward new land, new buildings, power infrastructure, or fit-out of existing shells. It does not separate AI-specific construction from general cloud expansion, and it does not track private operators outside the SEC filing universe. The sibling metrics on this page, colocation rental rates and critical equipment lead times, address parts of that gap, but the capex figure alone cannot tell a reader which binding constraint, land, power, or long-lead equipment, is actually slowing the build.
